correctness.rationale: Every automorphism has a unique constrained mixed-modulus matrix with two nonzero residue diagonal entries. Equality of products reduces to three and only three F_p congruences. The exhaustive cases x≠0, x=0 and (u,v)≠0, x=u=v=0 give centralizers (p−1)^2 p^(b−1), (p−1)p^b, and |G|. Their corresponding class sizes are p^2, p(p−1), and 1; element counts divided by these sizes yield the claimed multiplicities and their sum. Seven direct full automorphism-centralizer enumerations corroborated the result; mathematical proof covers every prime and b≥2.

originality.rationale: The full six-page 2006 Hillar–Rhea paper supplies the integer-matrix normal form and automorphism-group order only, not a conjugacy-class spectrum or commuting probability. The five-page Mann (2008) paper treats general structural constraints on class sizes, not the class-count multiplicities of this mixed-cyclic automorphism family. Searches of published findings, literature, tables, aliases, and stronger parameter coverage returned related fixed-point and involution censuses but not a statement whose conclusion implies all three new class multiplicities. The 1907 Ranum article is a plausible old antecedent with accessible metadata but unavailable full text, creating a limited residual priority risk.

value.rationale: The theorem gives the complete class-size distribution (not merely a new isolated coefficient) and thereby the number of irreducible characters and exact commuting probability of Aut(C_p⊕C_(p^b)) for an infinite family. Stability of cp under unbounded growth of the second exponent and the exact maximal 5/8 phenomenon for p=2 provide clear structural motivation. This invariant is not supplied by the known total-order formula; no extension beyond first exponent one is claimed.
